# OBS010 `arithmetic-if`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

An arithmetic `if (x) l1, l2, l3`.

## Why

The arithmetic IF branches on the sign of an expression to one of three labels. It was deleted in
Fortran 2018. Use a block `if` / `select case`.

## Reported

```fortran
if (x) 10, 20, 30
```

## Preferred

```fortran
if (x < 0) then
  ...
else if (x == 0) then
  ...
end if
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS010] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS010` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `OB081` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
